title: Affine charts and unchanged finite-Tor constructible input models
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme, with no separatedness assumption. Let $K,M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, with cohomology respectively zero outside integer intervals $[r,s]$ and $[t,u]$, and suppose $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, where $a\le b$.

There is a finite affine open covering $(j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow X)_{i\in I}$ such that every $U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and of finite type. For every $i$, the exact site restriction gives $K_i=j_i^*K\in D^b_{ctf}(U_{i,\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M_i=j_i^*M\in D^b_c(U_{i,\mathrm{et}},A)$ with the same cohomological intervals and with Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ for $K_i$. A constructible stratification of any $\mathcal H^h(K)$ or $\mathcal H^h(M)$ restricts, by intersection with $U_i$ and deletion of empty strata, to one of its restricted cohomology sheaf.

More precisely, there exists a cochain complex $P$ of flat $A_X$-module sheaves, zero outside $[a,b]$, and an isomorphism $K\cong Q_XP$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, where $Q_X$ is cochain localization. For every such representing isomorphism and every $i$, the restricted complex $P|_{U_i}$ has flat terms, is zero outside $[a,b]$, and its induced isomorphism is $K_i\cong Q_{U_i}(P|_{U_i})$. If $X$ is empty, the covering may be empty. Here Tor amplitude and $D^b_{ctf}$ use the etale-site convention of [lem-sf-flat-model].

proof.text: Use QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace and the finite subcover of X.affineCover, reindexed by Fintype.equivFin. An affine chart over the affine base is an affine morphism, so it is separated and quasi-compact. Open immersions are locally of finite type, and composition preserves this property. In the empty case choose Fin 0, so the empty-cover requirement is literal.

Exact categorical module-valued inverse image commutes with derived cohomology via the proved source mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso. This is the localization of exact-functor complex cohomology, using the exact-functor factorization. Apply map_isZero and transport along this isomorphism to preserve every stated bound. Convert finite-value constructibility with isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf, apply IsConstructibleSheaf.upperStar, and transport back by the same isomorphism. Unpack the given bounds to the standard derived t-structure when applying the source flat-model theorem.

Repeat the explicit stratification pullback construction for FiniteLocallyClosedStratification, indexing by the subtype of nonempty fibre products and reindexing it with Fintype.equivFin. The range formula Scheme.Pullback.range_snd identifies the new strata with the preimages. Every point in a preimage lifts to a fibre product by that formula, proving that deletion of the empty domains preserves covering. Local closedness, constructibility and pairwise disjointness pull back, and immersions are stable under base change. Finite locally constant module sheaves pull back. For each stratum, compose upperStarComp for the first projection, pullback.condition, and upperStarComp for the second projection, and finally the derived-cohomology comparison of step 2. These are isomorphisms in the categorical module-sheaf category, so all comparisons are module-linear without a separate ringed-module encoding bridge.

Apply the existing general small-etale hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_exists_flatModel to the global bounded constructible object, after the conversion in step 2. Unlike the specialized finite-coefficient wrapper, this source theorem does not require an invertibility instance. For any bounded flat representative, inverse image preserves flatness by upperStarPreservesFlat_moduleCat, proved from the geometric-fibre flatness criterion. The termwise image vanishes in the same degrees because the additive functor preserves zero objects. For any representing isomorphism e, take mapDerivedCategory.mapIso e followed by mapDerivedCategoryFactors.app P; choose this very isomorphism for the displayed equality.

On every chart, apply the reverse implication of the same general small-etale flat-model equivalence to its bounded constructibility from step 2 and the restricted global model from step 4. This proves the original Tor interval [a,b]. Combine this with the cover, both bounded-constructibility conclusions, both unchanged cohomology intervals, the chosen-stratification construction and the formula for every representing isomorphism. Empty-cover chart assertions are vacuous.

Edge cases checked: X empty, K=0, a=b, n=1, doubled-origin line, strata missing U_i. proof_deps equals the union of uses. No SGA appears. All 13 declared tool_uses are generic and accepted.
